name: Network Communities
summary: App to obtain the community structure of networks by using the Louvain or Infomap methods. All the Louvain quality functions work for networks with negative weights.

inputs.description: Input network. Note that not all the methods support negative weights, please use the Network Preprocessor app before running this App if the network has negative weights.

outputs.description: A network containing the detected community structure.

parameters.description:
Community detection method
- Louvain community detection algorithm, you can choose a variation by setting louvain-quality-function. Louvain quality functions works for negative weights.
- Infomap community detection algorithm.
- Stochastic block Model can handle layered networks, weighted, directed as well as negative weights.

options.label: Louvain
options.description: Louvain community detection algorithm, you can choose a variation by setting louvain-quality-function.

parameters.description: Number of trials for the Infomap community detection algorithm. (ignored if used for other methods)

Partition quality function to be optimized for the Louvain method:
- Modularity: Uses modularity optimization. Accepts weighted networks.
- RBConfiguration: Reichardt and Bornholdt’s Potts model with a configuration null model. Accepts weighted networks.
- RBER - Implements Reichardt and Bornholdt’s Potts model with an Erdős-Rényi null model. Accepts weighted networks.
- Clique Percolation Method (CPM) method. Accepts weighted networks.
- Significance: based on KL divergence comparing ER. Not suitable for weighted networks.
- Surprise: based on KL divergence. Works with weighted networks.

parameters.description: Defines the resolution parameter gamma for the quality functions.

If the network contains negative weights, the positive and negative partitions are weighted differently, according to Rubinov, Mikail, and Olaf Sporns. "Weight-conserving characterization of complex functional brain networks." Neuroimage 56, no. 4 (2011): 2068-2079. This seems to be appropriate when analyzing brain networks.
